title: Remove the Container Apps part of a PIM Manager environment (keep the data)
purpose: Removes the Container Apps part of one PIM Manager environment (every Container Apps job and app and the Container Apps environment in the resource group, plus the Azure role assignments held by their system identities) so the environment can be deployed again with a different exposure. Data is kept: the SQL database, the registry, Key Vault, storage, the VNet, the user-assigned identities and Log Analytics. It only lists what it would remove unless -Apply is given.
whenToRun: Before redeploying an environment with the other exposure (for example public to private, the 'remove and redeploy' route), or to remove the Container Apps part while keeping the data. It is part of the PIM Manager release package (it loads the engine's REST libraries next to it): run it from the package folder that Install-Invardia or the guided install downloaded (signed), or, for Community, from the public repository at the release tag. Then run Invoke-PimDeployAll.ps1 with the new exposure.

runAs.name: Owner, or Contributor + User Access Administrator
runAs.scope: the PIM resource group (role assignments: the subscription)
runAs.why: Deletes the Container Apps jobs, apps and environment, and the Azure role assignments of their system identities. Signed in through the browser or the Invardia Support app session (no Azure CLI, no modules).

changes.object: every Microsoft.App/jobs and Microsoft.App/containerApps resource, then the Microsoft.App/managedEnvironments resource (all listed first)
changes.why: The internal/external setting of a Container Apps environment cannot be changed; the stack is rebuilt by the next deploy.
changes.undo: Run Invoke-PimDeployAll.ps1 with the install's parameters (the saved deploy profile): it recreates the environment, the PIM Manager and the jobs and grants the new identities again.

changes.object: the Azure role assignments whose principal is one of those apps' or jobs' system identities
changes.why: They would be orphaned once the identities are deleted.
changes.undo: The next deploy grants the new identities their Azure roles again.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The PIM subscription. Every call names it explicitly; a sign-in that cannot see it is refused.

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The PIM resource group whose Container Apps stack is removed.

parameters.name: Apply
parameters.help: Delete. Without it (and always with -WhatIf) the script only lists the jobs, apps, environment and role assignments it would remove.

readsOnly: the resources in the resource group (Microsoft.App/* only are acted on)
each job's and app's system identity
the Azure role assignments of those identities
whatIf: Lists every Container Apps job, app and environment in the resource group with its system identity, and the role assignments of those identities, then prints 'PLAN ONLY: <n> job(s), <n> app(s), <n> environment(s), <n> role assignment(s)'. -WhatIf wins over -Apply ('-WhatIf: plan only -- -Apply is ignored'). Nothing is deleted.
undo: Run Invoke-PimDeployAll.ps1 with the install's parameters: it recreates the Container Apps environment, the PIM Manager and the jobs on the kept SQL database, registry and VNet, and grants the new identities again.
